topic: Experiential Memory for AI Agents: Research Update September 2026

findings.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems
findings.key_findings: Introduces a meta-evolutionary framework that jointly evolves agents' experiential knowledge AND their memory architecture. MemEvolve evaluates alternative memory designs during task solving and progressively selects more effective ones. Includes EvolveLab, a unified codebase distilling 12 representative memory systems into a modular design space (encode, store, retrieve, manage). Achieves up to 17.06% performance gains over frameworks like SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher on four challenging agentic benchmarks, with strong cross-task generalization.

findings.title: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
findings.key_findings: Proposes a non-parametric RL approach where a frozen LLM self-evolves via reinforcement learning on episodic memory. Structures memory as Intent-Experience-Utility triplets and applies Bellman updates to learn retrieval policies. Uses Two-Phase Retrieval: Phase A semantic similarity filtering, Phase B Q-value assessment for utility. Decouples stable reasoning (frozen LLM) from plastic memory. Achieves 69.7% cumulative success on ALFWorld vs 45.6% for strong memory baselines, demonstrating continuous runtime improvement without weight updates or catastrophic forgetting.

findings.title: MAGMA: A Multi-Graph based Agentic Memory Architecture for AI Agents
findings.key_findings: Introduces a multi-graph architecture organizing memory as a time-variant directed multigraph with four distinct relation dimensions: semantic, temporal, causal, and entity relations. Event-nodes capture content, timestamp, validity, and attribution. Uses intent-aware retrieval and dual-stream evolution balancing deep reasoning with efficiency. Represents shift from associative memory to structured, mechanism-dependent memory architecture. Addresses limitations of single flat databases and enables transparent, controllable long-term context management.

findings.title: EverMemOS: A Self-Organizing Memory Operating System for Structured Long-Horizon Reasoning
findings.key_findings: Implements an engram-inspired memory lifecycle: (1) Episodic Trace Formation converts dialogue into MemCells with atomic facts and time-bounded foresight signals; (2) Semantic Consolidation organizes MemCells into thematic MemScenes, distilling stable structures and updating user profiles; (3) Reconstructive Recollection performs MemScene-guided agentic retrieval. Outperforms SOTA on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and PersonaMem-v2, with particular strength in multi-hop and temporal questions requiring integration of dispersed evidence.

findings.title: BREW: Bootstrapping expeRientially-learned Environmental knoWledge
findings.key_findings: Distills an agent's past interaction trajectories into modular, human-interpretable environmental knowledge guided by rubrics and task-specific graders. Partitions raw experience into reusable knowledge units that capture domain-specific conventions, tool behaviors, and environmental dynamics. Enables agents to bootstrap understanding of new environments without extensive manual engineering. Demonstrates that experiential knowledge distillation transfers across tasks and improves sample efficiency in web navigation and coding domains.

findings.title: ReMe (Remember Me, Refine Me): A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution
findings.key_findings: Addresses the 'passive accumulation' paradigm where memory is treated as static append-only archive. Introduces a comprehensive framework across the memory lifecycle: dynamic construction, selective refinement, and utility-driven pruning. ReMe innovates with procedural memory that internalizes 'how-to' knowledge, reducing redundant trial-and-error. Uses experience-driven evolution where memory is continuously updated, corrected, and deprecated. Empirical evaluation on TravelPlanner and ALFWorld shows steadily higher success rates and greater efficiency as the memory repository is refined.

findings.title: ERL: Experiential Reflective Learning for Self-Improving LLM Agents
findings.venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop on Memory for LLM-Based Agentic Systems
findings.key_findings: Introduces a two-stage framework: (1) Heuristic Generation reflects on single-attempt task trajectories and outcomes to distill concise, actionable 'heuristics' capturing strategic principles; (2) Retrieval-Augmented Execution retrieves relevant heuristics at test time based on current task and injects them into context. Achieves 56.1% success rate on Gaia2 benchmark, a 7.8% improvement over ReAct baseline, with large gains in reliability (Pass^3). Heuristics generalize better than raw trajectories and failures are the best teachers for search.

findings.title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents
findings.key_findings: Reframes memory management as a set of learnable and evolvable 'memory skills' (e.g., 'Capture Temporal Context', 'Track Object Location'). Uses a Controller-Executor-Designer architecture: Controller selects relevant skills per span, Executor produces skill-guided memories, Designer reviews hard cases and evolves the skill bank by proposing refinements and new skills. Shifts from turn-level hand-designed operations to span-level skill-conditioned generation. Evaluated on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, HotpotQA, and ALFWorld with significant improvements and strong generalization.

findings.title: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
findings.key_findings: Builds a hierarchical skill library (SkillBank) through experience-based distillation, with adaptive retrieval for general and task-specific heuristics. Introduces a recursive evolution mechanism where the skill library co-evolves with the agent's policy during RL. Significantly reduces token footprint while enhancing reasoning utility. Demonstrates that skills discovered and evolved through experience transfer across tasks and enable more efficient exploration in complex environments.

findings.title: AdaMEM: Test-Time Adaptive Memory for Language Agents
findings.key_findings: Hybrid memory architecture maintaining long-term trajectory memory (offline collected raw experiences) and dynamic short-term strategy memory (generated on-the-fly). Adapts agent behavior at test time without parameter updates. Implements Step-MFT (Step-wise Memory Fine-Tuning) to train policy to synthesize high-quality strategies from retrieved experiences. Achieves up to 13% relative gains on ALFWorld and 11% on WebShop, with consistent leading performance on HotpotQA. Establishes a new scaling dimension for agentic memory supporting continuous reasoning and self-evolution.

findings.title: Evo-Memory: Benchmarking LLM Agent Test-time Learning with Self-Evolving Memory
findings.key_findings: Introduces a benchmark specifically modeling the structure and updates of agent memory during test-time learning, filling a gap left by LifelongAgentBench. Evaluates how memory structure evolves and impacts agent performance over extended interaction horizons. Provides standardized evaluation for self-evolving memory systems beyond static retrieval benchmarks.

findings.title: MARS: Memory-Enhanced Agents with Reflective Self-improvement
findings.key_findings: Three-agent framework (User, Assistant, Checker) integrating iterative feedback, reflective mechanisms, and Ebbinghaus forgetting curve-based memory optimization. Enhances self-adjustment and memory management in complex tasks. Shows significant improvements on AgentBench for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and open-source models. Reduces basic errors and logical mistakes through self-evolution. Extends to multi-agent MARS with distributed introspective functions across specialized subagents (critics, judges, supervisors).

findings.title: REMT: Real-time Editable Memory Topology
findings.key_findings: Focuses on dynamic edge updates in memory topology driven by affective salience, not merely accumulating stored entries. Creates a closed feedback loop between affective weighting and graph restructuring. Emergent properties include continuity across sessions, mood-modulated retrieval, and individualized behavioral adaptation driven by structural memory dynamics rather than explicit scripting. Represents a shift from passive logging to topology-level adaptation.

findings.title: MemGen: Weaving Generative Latent Memory for Self-Evolving Agents
findings.key_findings: Introduces generative latent memory that weaves experience into compressed, reusable latent representations. Enables self-evolving agents to maintain long-term coherence while continuously updating internal world models. Demonstrates improved sample efficiency and transfer in long-horizon tasks.

findings.title: AgentEvolver: Towards Efficient Self-Evolving Agent System
findings.key_findings: Proposes a scalable self-evolving distributed memory system (SEDM) for multi-agent environments. Addresses the challenge of coordinating memory evolution across agent populations. Demonstrates efficient self-improvement through distributed experience sharing and consensus-based memory updates.

findings.title: Memory in the Age of AI Agents (Survey)
findings.key_findings: Landmark survey from NUS, Renmin University, Fudan University, and others providing the 'Forms-Functions-Dynamics' framework for AI agent memory. Analyzes token-level, parametric, and latent memory architectures. Covers 100+ papers across memory substrate, cognitive mechanisms (sensory, working, episodic, semantic, procedural), and memory subject (user-centric vs agent-centric). Establishes unified taxonomy and identifies meta-evolution as critical frontier.

findings.title: A Survey of Agent Memory in the Second Half: Towards Self-Evolving and Long-Horizon Agents
findings.key_findings: Unified view across three dimensions: memory substrate (internal parametric + external RAG), cognitive mechanism (sensory, working, episodic, semantic, procedural), and memory subject (user-centric personalization vs agent-centric experience). Analyzes single/multi-agent topologies and learning policies over memory operations. 50+ authors from major institutions. Highlights memory as the substrate through which agents self-evolve: short-term memory gates experience abstraction, long-term memory consolidates into reusable knowledge/skills.

findings.title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve
findings.key_findings: First systematic comprehensive review of self-evolving agents. Categorizes evolution targets: prompts, memory, skills, tools, model behavior, meta-level control. Identifies barriers: longitudinal evaluation, transfer, verification, safety governance. Frames self-improvement as a 'trace-to-capability' problem: capture experience, assign to update surface, verify value, preserve control. Historical progression from episodic tool-use loops to cross-task reuse to persistent harness-centered runtimes with evolvable memory, workflows, skills, and feedback channels.

summary: As of September 2026, experiential memory for AI agents has matured from passive storage to dynamic, self-evolving systems. Key trends: (1) Meta-evolution frameworks (MemEvolve) now jointly optimize memory content AND architecture; (2) Multi-graph/hypergraph structures (MAGMA, EverMemOS) replace flat vector stores with mechanism-dependent relations; (3) Procedural memory (ReMe, MemSkill, SkillRL) treats 'how-to' knowledge as evolvable skills with controller-executor-designer loops; (4) Experiential reflective learning (ERL, MARS) distills trajectories into transferable heuristics, outperforming raw trajectory replay; (5) Environmental knowledge bootstrapping (BREW) extracts modular, interpretable world models from interaction traces; (6) Test-time adaptive memory (AdaMEM, Evo-Memory benchmark) enables continuous adaptation without weight updates via hybrid long-term/short-term memory; (7) Major surveys (Memory in the Age of AI Agents, Agent Memory in the Second Half, Self-Evolving Agents survey) establish unified taxonomies and identify meta-evolution as the critical frontier; (8) Self-evolving agents (MemRL, AgentEvolver, MemGen) demonstrate sustained improvement on benchmarks (ALFWorld 69.7% vs 45.6%, Gaia2 56.1%) through non-parametric RL on episodic memory and generative latent memory. The field has converged on a three-tier cognitive architecture (episodic/semantic/procedural) with memory as the substrate for lifelong self-evolution.
